source: Coach Mode plain words (CD-009). Written for someone who has never looked at a payslip: short sentences, common words. The wording for dates of birth, pay, home, debt and savings follows SPARKS' owner-approved data/sketch_help.json.
confidenceNote: Words, not figures. The 'good' lines are the common guides (3 to 6 months of cushion, 28% on housing, 20% saved) and say so; nothing here is a number the app computes.
note: fields: one entry a field id in data/fields.json (plain, means, look, unsure, example). readouts: one a read-out id in data/session_paths.json (label, what, good). stops: one a stop (title, intro, done). words: [term, plain], the glossary.

dob.means: Your age. It sets every date, like the year work could become a choice.
dob.look: Your driver's licence, or the birthday your phone already knows.
dob.unsure: The month and year are enough. Pick the first of the month if you do not know the day.

dependents.plain: How many people count on your money?
dependents.means: Kids, or anyone else you support. More people means a bigger cushion.
dependents.look: Count them. Do not count yourself, or a partner who earns.
dependents.unsure: If nobody, type 0. That is a real answer.

grossAnnualIncome.plain: How much are you paid in a year, before anything is taken out?
grossAnnualIncome.means: The big number your job talks about. Tax has not come out of it yet.
grossAnnualIncome.look: Your offer letter, or the word 'gross' on a payslip. Paid by the hour? Your rate, times the hours you really work, times 52.
grossAnnualIncome.unsure: Leave it blank. We can work it out from what lands in your account.

takeHomeMonthly.plain: How much money lands in your account each month?
takeHomeMonthly.means: What you are paid after tax and everything else comes out. Your life runs on this number.
takeHomeMonthly.look: Open your bank app. Add up what came in from your job over the last month.
takeHomeMonthly.unsure: Use a normal month, not the best one. Rough is fine.

payVaries.plain: Does your pay change a lot from month to month?
payVaries.means: Pay that jumps around needs a bigger cushion.
payVaries.look: Look at your last three paydays in your bank app. If they are close, say no.
payVaries.unsure: If they were within about a hundred dollars of each other, say no.

accommodationMonthly.plain: What do you pay for your home each month?
accommodationMonthly.means: Rent, or the mortgage payment. If tax and home insurance are inside that payment, include them.
accommodationMonthly.look: Your rent agreement, or the one payment that leaves your account for the mortgage.
accommodationMonthly.unsure: If you split the home with someone, type your share. If you pay nothing, type 0: that is a real answer.

foodMonthly.plain: What does food cost you in a month?
foodMonthly.look: Most bank apps can total a month of grocery and restaurant spending.
foodMonthly.unsure: Nobody knows this to the dollar. A rough number beats a blank.

transportationMonthly.plain: What does getting around cost in a month?
transportationMonthly.means: Gas, fares, parking, car insurance, repairs. Not the car loan payment: that goes with debts.
transportationMonthly.look: Your bank app, for a normal month.
transportationMonthly.unsure: Rough is fine. Tick 'this is a guess'.

wantsMonthly.plain: Roughly, what does everything else cost in a month?
wantsMonthly.means: Phone, internet, subscriptions, clothes, haircuts, gifts, fun. Not rent, food, getting around, loan payments, or money you put away.
wantsMonthly.look: Your bank app. Or add it up in pieces.
wantsMonthly.unsure: Take a guess and tick 'this is a guess'. You can sharpen it later.

hasDebt.plain: Do you owe money to anyone?
hasDebt.means: Cards, a car loan, student loans, buy now pay later, money owed to family.
hasDebt.look: Each card or loan app shows a balance.
hasDebt.unsure: If you pay your card off in full every month and owe nothing today, say no.

cashSavings.plain: How much money is in the bank, all together?
cashSavings.means: Checking and savings: money you could spend today.
cashSavings.look: Your bank app: the balance on the first screen. Add every account.
cashSavings.unsure: Nearest hundred is fine. Or list each account on the 'What you own' stop instead.

investments.plain: How much is invested, all together?
investments.means: Money in the market: a retirement plan at work, an IRA, an investing app.
investments.look: Your retirement or investing app. A 401(k) at work counts, even if you never look at it.
investments.unsure: Nearest thousand is fine. Or list each account on the 'What you own' stop.

highestDeductible.plain: What is the most you would have to pay before insurance kicks in?
highestDeductible.means: Your biggest deductible: health, car or home. The first thing a cash cushion has to cover.
highestDeductible.look: Your health plan card or app, under 'deductible'.
highestDeductible.unsure: Leave it blank if you do not know.

termLife.plain: How much life insurance do you have?
termLife.means: The amount paid out if you died. Often it comes through work.
termLife.look: Your benefits page at work, or the policy.
termLife.unsure: If nobody depends on your money, you may not need any. Leave it blank if unsure.

disabilityMonthly.plain: If you could not work, what would you get each month?
disabilityMonthly.means: Disability insurance pays part of your pay if you get sick or hurt. Often it comes through work.
disabilityMonthly.look: Your benefits page at work: 'long-term disability'.
disabilityMonthly.unsure: Leave it blank if you do not know.

employerMatch.plain: Does your employer add money when you save for retirement?
employerMatch.means: A match is free money. '50% up to 6%' means: for every dollar you put in, up to 6% of your pay, they add 50 cents.
employerMatch.look: Your benefits page, or HR. Two numbers: how much they match, and up to what share of your pay.
employerMatch.unsure: Ask HR: 'do you match my 401(k), and how much?'

contributionPercent.plain: What share of your pay goes to retirement?
contributionPercent.means: The percent taken from each paycheck into your 401(k) or similar.
contributionPercent.look: Your payslip, or the retirement plan app.
contributionPercent.unsure: Type 0 if nothing goes in. That is a real answer.

filingStatus.plain: How do you file your taxes?
filingStatus.means: Single, married filing together, and so on. It sets your tax rate.
filingStatus.look: The top of last year's tax return.
filingStatus.unsure: Most single people file single. Most married couples file together.

state.plain: Which state do you live in?
state.means: Your state has its own tax rate.
state.unsure: Where you live now, not where you came from.

marginalRate.plain: What is your tax rate on the next dollar you earn?
marginalRate.means: Your marginal rate. It says how much of a raise, or of a pretax saving, is really tax.
marginalRate.look: Your coach can read it off your pay and how you file. Or the tax return.
marginalRate.unsure: Leave it blank. We work it out from your pay.

debtType.plain: What kind of debt is it?
debtType.means: Credit cards cost the most. Student loans and mortgages usually cost less.

debtBalance.plain: How much do you still owe on it?
debtBalance.means: The whole balance, not the monthly payment.
debtBalance.look: The balance on the first screen of the app.
debtBalance.unsure: Rough is fine. Tick 'this is a guess'.

debtRate.plain: What interest rate does it charge?
debtRate.means: The yearly percent, often called APR. Higher means it costs more to keep.
debtRate.look: On the statement, often near the bottom: 'APR'. Cards are often 20 to 30.
debtRate.unsure: Leave it blank. It can be added later.

debtMinPayment.plain: What is the smallest payment it asks for each month?
debtMinPayment.means: The minimum. Not what you would like to pay.
debtMinPayment.look: The statement: 'minimum payment'. A car or student loan has one fixed payment.
debtMinPayment.unsure: Leave it blank if you do not know.

assetAccountType.plain: What kind of account is it?
assetAccountType.means: It says whether the money is cash you can spend, or invested for later, and how it is taxed.
assetAccountType.look: The app: checking, savings, 401(k), IRA, brokerage.

assetValue.plain: How much is in it right now?
assetValue.look: The first screen of the app.

goalName.means: Something you want money for, with a date.
goalName.look: Nothing to look up. Say it in your own words.

goalDate.plain: When do you want it by?
goalDate.means: The date. It sets how much a month it takes.
goalDate.look: Nothing to look up. A rough date is fine.
goalDate.unsure: Pick a year and the first of a month.

goalAmount.plain: About how much will it cost?
goalAmount.means: The whole cost, in today's money.
goalAmount.look: A quick search, or a number you have heard.
goalAmount.unsure: Rough is fine. Tick 'this is a guess'.

goalSaved.plain: How much have you saved for it so far?
goalSaved.means: Money already set aside for this goal.
goalSaved.look: The savings account you use for it.

goalMonthly.plain: How much goes toward it each month?
goalMonthly.means: What you already put away for it, on purpose.
goalMonthly.look: A transfer in your bank app.

savingsRate.label: How much you keep
savingsRate.what: Of what you earn, the share you do not spend. Saved money is what buys freedom later.
savingsRate.good: 10% is a start. 20% is strong. 30% and up is fast.

debtToIncome.label: Pay going to debt
debtToIncome.what: Of your monthly pay before tax, the share that goes to debt payments.
debtToIncome.good: Under 20% is comfortable. Over 36% is a squeeze.

emergencyFundMonths.label: Months of cushion
emergencyFundMonths.what: How many months your cash in the bank would cover if pay stopped.
emergencyFundMonths.good: 3 months is the floor. 6 is calm.

liquidityRatio.label: Months you could reach
liquidityRatio.what: Like the cushion, but counting everything you could turn into cash quickly.

housingRatio.label: Home as a share of pay
housingRatio.what: Of your pay before tax, the share that goes on rent or the mortgage.

netWorth.label: What you own minus what you owe
netWorth.what: Everything you own, minus every debt. The one number that shows the whole picture.
netWorth.good: Going up over time is what matters, not the number today.

takeHome.label: What lands each month
takeHome.what: Pay after tax and deductions, a month.

surplus.label: Left over each month
surplus.what: What lands, minus what a month costs. This is the money that pays for goals.

spending.label: What a month costs
spending.what: Home, food, getting around and everything else, added up.

debtFree.label: Debt-free in
debtFree.what: How long until every debt is gone, paying only the minimums. Paying extra makes it shorter.

invested.label: Invested
invested.what: Money in the market, growing for later.

marginalRate.label: Tax on the next dollar
marginalRate.what: Of the next dollar you earn, the share that goes to tax. It says what a raise, or a pretax saving, is really worth.

goalsMonthly.label: All goals, a month
goalsMonthly.what: What every goal needs each month, added up, to land on time.
goalsMonthly.good: Fits inside what is left over each month.

fiDate.label: The work-optional date
fiDate.what: When what you have saved could pay for life without a paycheck. Three cases: good, likely, slow.
fiDate.good: Sooner is nice, but the direction matters more: it moves when you save more or spend less.

life.title: The big picture
life.intro: Start with what they want, not with numbers. Three goals with rough dates is enough. Write them the way the client says them.

income.title: Money coming in
income.intro: One number matters most: what lands in the account each month. Get that first. The before-tax number can wait.
income.done: We know what lands each month, even roughly.

spending.title: Money going out
spending.intro: Four boxes: home, food, getting around, everything else. Rough is fine. Then look at what is left.
spending.done: We know what is left at the end of a normal month.

debt.title: What you owe
debt.intro: List every debt. The balance and the rate matter most; the minimum payment sets the pace. Then look at when they are gone.
debt.done: Every debt is listed and the debt-free date shows.

safety.title: The cushion
safety.intro: How long could they go if pay stopped? Cash in the bank first, then the insurance that protects the rest.
safety.done: We know how many months the cushion covers, and what is missing.

assets.title: What you own
assets.intro: Every account with money in it. The kind matters: cash you can spend, or money invested for later.
assets.done: We can see the whole picture: owned minus owed.

taxes.title: Taxes
taxes.intro: Two facts set the rate: how they file and where they live. Then one easy win, like a pretax contribution.
taxes.done: We know the tax on the next dollar, and one move to try.

goals.title: Goals and the map
goals.intro: Put a price and a date on each goal. The app says what each needs a month and whether it fits.
goals.done: Every goal has a monthly number and a status.

decisions.title: Big decisions
decisions.intro: The choices on their mind this year: a house, a car, a job, a move. Each one gets a verdict: go, wait, or no.

words: the work-optional date
The day work becomes a choice: what you have saved could pay for life without a paycheck.
coast
From this age, what is already invested grows to enough by itself. You could stop adding and still get there.
take-home pay
What lands in your account after tax and everything else comes out.
pay before tax
The big number your job talks about, before tax comes out. Also called gross pay.
net worth
Everything you own, minus everything you owe.
cushion
Cash in the bank that covers life if pay stops. Also called an emergency fund.
minimum payment
The smallest amount a card or loan asks for each month.
interest rate
The yearly percent a debt charges, or an account pays. Often written APR.
A retirement account through work. Money goes in before tax, often with a match from your employer.
IRA
A retirement account you open yourself. Roth means the tax was paid already.
high-yield savings
A savings account that pays more interest than a normal one. Still cash you can spend.
brokerage
An investing account with no special tax rules. You can take money out any time.
match
Money your employer adds when you save for retirement. Free money.
tax on the next dollar
Your marginal rate: of the next dollar you earn, the share that goes to tax.
a guess
A number typed roughly, to be checked later. The app shows it as rough until it is confirmed.
snapshot
A copy of all the numbers on a day, kept so a later day can be compared to it.
recap
The summary of a session: what we covered, what changed, homework.
check-in
A short monthly update: balances that moved, and how you feel about money.
homework
One thing to find or do before the next session.
verdict
Go, wait, or no on a big decision.
detour
Leaving the current stop for a moment, with a way straight back.
stop
One step on the path a session follows. Nine stops, in order, unless you skip or move them.
